subject: Post-call recap + next steps: dedicated capacity pricing & unit-econ check (BrightEdge AI)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@brightedge.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@brightedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: dedicated capacity pricing & unit-econ check (BrightEdge AI)

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — quick recap and the small list of follow-ups we promised. Goal: align on expected token volumes, budget envelope, and a recommended reserved GPU configuration so we can issue a firm quote.

Key points from the call:
- Current baseline: ~12M tokens/month across low-latency inference (retrieval-augmented generation for search assistants).
- 6–12 month projection: 50M tokens/mo (conservative) -> 180–220M tokens/mo (upside).
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 200ms for single-turn queries, p50 << 100ms is desirable.
- Concurrency/throughput target: support 400–1,200 concurrent short requests (avg 80 tokens/request) — translates roughly to 32k–96k tokens/sec peak depending on batching.
- Budget band you shared: ~$20k–$80k/month for dedicated inference (inclusive of reserved capacity). You flagged procurement constraints for Q1.
- GPU preferences: open to H100 if needed for perf, but cost-sensitive — A100-80GB or L40s may be acceptable with quantization/optimized kernels.

Immediate asks (what we need from you to produce a formal quote):
1) Confirm target tokens/month range to price unit-econ slices (pick conservative and upside numbers).
2) Clarify strict latency SLO (95th percentile) and whether batching can be used for non-interactive workloads.
3) Any compliance/KMS notes that would push toward Private deployment?

Proposed Redwood options we'll price in the quote (range):
- Option A (cost-optimized): 4 x A100-80GB reserved, optimized kernels + prefix cache — expected baseline throughput ~45k tokens/sec, ~$X per GPU-mo (will show $/1M tokens).
- Option B (latency-first): 2 x H100 reserved (or 1 H100 + 2 A100), lower p95 latency at higher cost.
- Option C (burst + reserved): 2 reserved A100 + burst pool & auto-fallback to hosted — smaller committed spend, higher burst charges.

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Estimate-v3.xlsx (high-level cost model), draft SOW (separate doc).

Next steps:
- I’ll pull together a concise quote with unit-econ lines ($/1M tokens) for the three options above and a recommended starting config based on your confirmed token targets.
- Please confirm the numbers in section “Key inputs” of the attached sheet and reply with any procurement calendar constraints.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@brightedge.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@brightedge.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: dedicated capacity pricing & unit-econ check (BrightEdge AI)

Appreciate the clear recap. Couple clarifications and the numbers you asked for below.

Confirmed volumes:
- Starting baseline (month 1–3): 40–50M tokens/month (we’ll have an initial pilot traffic spike but expect it to settle).
- Scale target (6–12 months): 150–200M tokens/month if adoption goes well.

Latency SLO:
- For our customer-facing assistant, we need 95th <= 150ms. For background batch generation (recommendations pipeline) latency can be relaxed. Batching is fine for background workloads, but production queries must hit the low-latency path.

Concurrency/throughput:
- User traffic profile: many short, low-token requests (median ~60 tokens). Peak concurrency target ~800 concurrent short requests.

Budget:
- Internal procurement band for committed spend: $25k–$60k/month. If the unit-econ for $/1M tokens can show <$100/1M tokens at committed volume, we’re in good shape.

GPU preference:
- We prefer to avoid H100 unless necessary — if Redwood can meet latency with 4x A100 + tuning, that will be more likely to pass procurement. If H100 is materially better for p95 under our concurrency profile, we can discuss.

Procurement timing:
- We’ll kick procurement in early Jan; would like a final quote and SOW by Dec 8 if possible.

Thanks,
Sandeep
CTO, BrightEdge AI
sandeep@brightedge.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@brightedge.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@brightedge.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: dedicated capacity pricing & unit-econ check (BrightEdge AI)

Thanks Sandeep — this is super helpful and aligns well with what Jordan and I sketched. Quick note on how we’ll structure the quote and the asks we’ve taken on: 

What we’ll include in the December 8 quote: 
- Two committed configurations (price for monthly reserved capacity + expected $/1M tokens at your conservative and upside volumes):
  * Cost-optimized baseline: 4 x A100-80GB reserved, tuned runtime + caching (target ~$75–95 / 1M tokens at 150–200M committed tokens).
  * Latency-focused: 2 x H100 reserved (or hybrid mix), lower p95 — premium pricing (we’ll show delta).
- A hybrid burst option that combines 2 reserved A100 + burst credit to hosted for scaling peaks (smaller commitment).
- Clear line items: reserved infra, burst usage, data egress, support/observability add-ons, and a recommended trial period (45 days) for tuning.

Technical follow-ups for Ben (cc’d): 
- Ben: can you validate the p95 testing approach with 800 concurrent short requests and confirm our estimated tokens/sec for 4x A100? Please include expected p95 numbers after prefix caching and kernel optimizations.

Procurement / contract notes: 
- We’ll prepare a draft SOW and standard terms; for procurement we can offer a 60-day window to sign with the provided quote. Any specific legal or SOC/KMS requirements, flag them now so we can include in the SOW.

Call to action:
- Sandeep/Elena: confirm the conservative (40–50M) and target (150–200M) pick that you want priced, and whether you’d prefer we prioritize the A100-cost baseline or include H100 as the default.
- I’ll aim to have the XLS cost model and SOW in your inbox by EOD Dec 6 so Jordan can review before we finalize on Dec 8.

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: dedicated capacity pricing & unit-econ check (BrightEdge AI)

Thanks all — we’re aligned. Confirming the two volume points to be priced: conservative = 50M tokens/mo, target = 175M tokens/mo.

Preference: Please prioritize the A100 baseline in the proposal (we’ll consider H100 if the numbers show a meaningful latency improvement for p95 under our concurrency).

Procurement ask: include a standard data processing addendum and KMS integration note in the SOW. We’ll involve procurement/prod security once the Dec 8 quote is in hand.
